Queries target established knowledge on how operation effects depend on the surrounding operations in NAS-Bench-201 cells:

1. **Operation interactions and connectivity.** Whether removing an edge (none) or adding a skip_connect matters depends on whether other paths from input to output survive. Gradient flow and path-length effects in DAG cells are relevant here.
2. **Skip-connect and pooling behavior.** Skip connections are known to help optimization in some contexts and to dominate in others (e.g., DARTS collapse). Their benefit may depend on whether parallel edges already carry convolutions.
3. **Convolution kernel size and receptive-field effects in cells.** Whether swapping nor_conv_1x1 and nor_conv_3x3 helps depends on what other operations are on the same paths, because receptive field and parameter count accumulate along paths.
